turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hey, come on back. You look like the waiting room wore you out.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): It did. And the parking. Can we just get to it.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sure. What's the main problem today?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Stomach cramps. And my bowels are a mess.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tell me what the cramps do.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): They're low, more on the left. A grabby pain. When I pass stool they ease off. Been a year.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): The bowels, what's the mess exactly?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): I go constipated for days, then it's loose, then constipated again. Whole year, same as the cramps. And I'm bloated most afternoons, worse when work goes crazy.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): What do you do for work, if that's the trigger?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Project manager at a logistics firm. Stress is basically the job. It never turns off.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm 46 and I feel like my body just quit on me. Don't need a lecture, okay.

[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): No lecture. Let me say it back. Left-sided cramps that get better after a bowel movement, bloating most afternoons, constipation trading off with loose stool, all for a year, and work stress makes the bloating worse.
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. You got it. Finally.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the toilet, or black stool?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I checked more than once. No blood.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any weight loss?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No. If anything I'm up a little from sitting at a desk. I have not lost weight.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fevers? Chills?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm. I don't know. I get hot sitting at my desk but the vents are broken, and I never stuck a thermometer in, so maybe, maybe not.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Okay, fever's a maybe, we'll leave it. Have you vomited?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No vomiting. I do get queasy when the cramp hits, but it passes.

[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Top of my list is a sensitive gut, irritable bowel, especially with the stress and the way the pain eases when you go. I will not put that down as final today. I also can't rule out celiac, or a thyroid problem, from the story alone.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Wonderful. So nobody knows. What now, more pills?
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Maybe not more pills. What are you on already?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodipine for the pressure, five milligrams every morning.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mm. Next?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): The cholesterol one at night. It's simvastaten, twenty milligrams. And sugar tablets, metformin, five hundred milligrams twice a day.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): So amlodipine five in the morning for the pressure, simvastatin twenty at night, metformin five hundred twice a day. Any shop remedies, teas, powders?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning. Half a teaspoon in water. Label's gone, I couldn't tell you the real name.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): My sister dumped it on me. I take it so she'll stop texting. It's probably nothing.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Keep the amlodipine, the simvastatin, and the metformin going just as you are. Hold the powder until we're clearer. I don't want a mystery mix in the background.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. Easy. I didn't like the taste anyway.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm going to order bloods. A blood count, a metabolic panel, thyroid tests, and a celiac screen. The lab here can draw you on the way out. I'll put the order in now.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): All of that today? Ugh. Okay. Stick me and let me leave.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): On the food side, keep a plain diary for the next two weeks, what you eat and what your gut does. And cut back on the usual agitators.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): I live on coffee. Four cups, easy, and a sad desk salad. That's lunch.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Four cups is a lot. Try bringing coffee down to one or two a day, and eat smaller meals, and see if the cramps settle. Not a punishment, just a trial.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): One or two. I'll try. I'm not gonna be nice about it.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's allowed. Come back in three weeks and we'll look at the labs and the diary together.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Three weeks. What if this gets ugly before then?
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): If you see blood, if you can't keep liquids down, or if the pain turns sharp and stays, don't sit on it. Urgent care or the ER. Otherwise three weeks is fine.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Got it. Blood, can't drink, pain that stays. ER. Thrilling.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): One quick look at your belly before you go, if you'll let me.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah yeah. Just don't poke the left side like you're mad at it.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Soft belly. Tender over the left lower side where you said, no rebound, bowel sounds are present.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): Ow. Yep. That's the spot. Are we done?
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): We're done for today. Labs on your way out, hold the powder, diary and less coffee, and I'll see you in three weeks.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Three weeks. If the diary is a mess of scribbles don't yell at me.
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): Scribbles are fine. As long as I can read the pattern. Take care, Ms. Hale.

spec.situation: Person with cramps relieved by passing stool, bloating, alternating constipation and loose stools for a year; stress at work; denies blood and weight loss after prompting; bloods planned, diet advice.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

features: doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

omissions.text: Possible fever/chills was asked about and not definitively denied: patient was unsure, saying maybe/maybe not and had not checked a temperature; doctor documented fever as a maybe.
Type 2 diabetes / elevated blood sugar is implied by current metformin use ('sugar tablets, metformin') but is not recorded in past medical history.
Plan for labs to be drawn today/on the way out at the lab here was stated.
Follow-up is specifically to review the labs and the food/gut diary together in three weeks.
